Tech Report: Ocarina of Time Remake Lets You Pull Off Lynel Trickshots Without Any Lynels

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If there's one thing The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom have taught us, it's that players will eventually find a way to turn even the simplest combat encounter into an opportunity for an unnecessarily impressive trickshot.
  • Apparently, that mindset isn't going anywhere, even when you take away the open-world freedom of those games, even when we are talking about a more contained gameplay like Ocarina of Time Remake.
  • A Japanese player recently shared an incredible clip of their own in the newest version of Ocarina of Time, taking down four ReDeads with only four carefully aimed Light Arrows!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there's one thing The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom have taught us, it's that players will eventually find a way to turn even the simplest combat encounter into an opportunity for an unnecessarily impressive trickshot.

Apparently, that mindset isn't going anywhere, even when you take away the open-world freedom of those games, even when we are talking about a more contained gameplay like Ocarina of Time Remake.

A Japanese player recently shared an incredible clip of their own in the newest version of Ocarina of Time, taking down four ReDeads with only four carefully aimed Light Arrows!

Instead of shooting directly at the enemies, Adult Link fires his arrow high into the sky, letting it travel through the air before hitting all four targets in sequence. The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course. Here, check it out:.

Recent findings suggest that the clip takes place in the destroyed Hyrule Market, just before the entrance to Ganon's Castle. It's already an impressive display of precision, but what makes it even better is how unnecessary the whole thing is. Link could probably deal with those ReDeads in a much simpler way. But where's the fun in that?

Recent findings suggest that after its publication, the video rapidly gained attention on social media, surpassing 750,000 views and 16,000 likes as we speak! Naturally, other Zelda fans were quick to praise the player's ridiculous display of skill, with one commenter calling it "one of the most impressive things I have ever seen," adding that the precision was an "absolute master class.".

Recent findings suggest that another player was equally impressed, writing, "Single-handedly the most impressive Zelda clip I ever seen." And honestly, it's hard to disagree! Pulling off a trickshot like this requires a surprising amount of patience and precision, especially when you're trying to hit multiple enemies with an arrow that wasn't even aimed directly at them.

The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course.

What's particularly fun about this discovery is how it shows that the spirit of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom lives on even in a much more structured adventure. Ocarina of Time doesn't offer the same level of freedom when it comes to approaching combat, but that hasn't stopped players from experimenting with its mechanics and finding creative ways to play.

The more recent games taught an entire generation of Zelda fans that almost every situation can become a playground if you're willing to experiment enough. Whether that's launching enemies into the air, using physics to solve problems in unexpected ways, creating weird machines, or spending far too long trying to land the perfect arrow, players have learned to make their own fun! And now, even without a single Lynel around, that same energy has found its way into Ocarina of Time. I guess some habits really do follow you from one Hyrule to another.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event.
  • Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.
  • The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

Recent findings suggest that the ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

It has been revealed that the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

In a recent development, heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

Sources indicate that we also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

#17455. Tech Report: GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (822 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: GTA 6 Breaks a 25-Year Tradition, and Rockstar Explains Why

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6.
  • This wasn't simply an overlooked feature.
  • In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6. One old activity, though, isn't making the cut. Players can no longer hire sex workers, ending a feature that's been part of the series since Grand Theft Auto 3 arrived in 2001.

This wasn't simply an overlooked feature. Rockstar deliberately left it out. Shacknews asked the GTA studio about it, and they confirmed the feature was removed. Rockstar also offered an explanation, and it comes down to the kind of story it wants to tell with Jason and Lucia.

In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run. The studio remarked it had considered which familiar GTA elements would work alongside the characters and the relationship at the center of the game, rather than bringing back every previous feature by default.

Rockstar pointed to systems such as police pursuits, radio stations, robberies, and car theft as examples of the elements it carried forward. Those all fit the criminal adventures Jason and Lucia get caught up in. Hiring sex workers, apparently, didn't fit what the team had in mind.

Recent findings suggest that it's an interesting explanation because Rockstar didn't claim the removal was due to a technical limitation or a ratings requirement. Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Sources indicate that anyone who's watched the GTA 6 launch trailer will have seen how much of the marketing revolves around the pair. Rockstar keeps bringing the focus back to Jason and Lucia, even when the trailers show off everything else happening in Leonida. Their story is the reason the two playable protagonists are together in the first place.

According to recent reports, hiring sex workers first became a recognizable open-world interaction in GTA 3, and it remained available across later mainline games, including Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5. For some players, it became one of those strange little things they expected to find when wandering around a GTA city at night.

It also brings back one of GTA 3's more infamous controversies. Players could hire a sex worker, kill her afterward, and pick up the money they'd just spent. That drew plenty of criticism at the time, and the mechanic stuck around. It was still possible in GTA 5.

Industry observers note that I can't help connecting this to Jason Schreier's 2022 Bloomberg report, which said Rockstar was trying to avoid jokes that punch down at marginalized groups. He suggested GTA 6 might feel quite different from GTA 5, and seeing this particular feature disappear makes me think he might have been onto something. Rockstar indicates it's about Jason and Lucia, of course, but I wonder if both things played a part.

Industry observers note that it was never the reason most people played these games, of course. But GTA has always made a point of filling its streets with activities that aren't strictly necessary for completing missions. The series' reputation comes as much from those distractions as it does from car chases, shootouts, and elaborate heists.

That's why removing a relatively minor interaction is still newsworthy. It has survived several generations of GTA, across different protagonists and settings. Now that Rockstar is putting two characters in a relationship at the heart of its newest game, that particular carryover has finally been dropped.

This doesn't mean GTA 6 has suddenly become a tame version of Grand Theft Auto. The game's nightlife is very much present. Our guide to GTA 6's strip clubs already covers several venues around Leonida, so the absence of one activity shouldn't be confused with the removal of adult entertainment altogether.

Recent findings suggest that there's a distinction between the atmosphere of Vice City and the specific actions Rockstar lets the protagonists take. A setting can still have strip clubs and the more outrageous side of GTA without including every interaction that existed in previous games.

The confirmation is also about a specific action players can take. It doesn't establish whether sex workers appear in the game as background characters, or whether the story mentions them. Rockstar answered a question about the gameplay interaction, not every possible appearance of the subject.

Recent findings suggest that some fans will probably find the change strange, particularly if they've been playing since the PS2 days. Others might not have noticed the feature was missing at all. Either way, it's one of the clearer examples of Rockstar choosing to leave an old mechanic behind instead of carrying it over simply because it's always been there.

For a series known for giving players countless ways to get distracted, that's a notable decision. And this time, at least, Rockstar has given a pretty straightforward reason for making it.

Recent findings suggest that nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

It has been revealed that nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Sources indicate that late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

In a recent development, that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a newly introduced brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

According to recent reports, seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his proposal.

Industry observers note that as for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as latest minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

Sources indicate that as you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with latest special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

In a recent development, beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

Major Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that friendslop du jour Significant Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!).
  • A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset.
  • Recent findings suggest that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that friendslop du jour Significant Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.".

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

Recent findings suggest that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Massive Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Massive Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest.".

Sources indicate that if I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Major Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:.

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together.".

In a recent development, shang-Chi first debuted in 2021's Shang Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, but as was recently teased by Marvel, we haven't really heard from him since. The character is now set to return to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, where he'll team up in the fight against Doctor Doom.

It's not clear if his absence will be addressed in the upcoming superhero movie, but in a fresh interview, actor Simu Liu has shared his head canon about where his character has been this whole time, and it actually makes a lot of sense.

Industry observers note that appearing on the Countdown to Doomsday podcast, Liu was asked about what he thinks Shang-Chi has been up to. After some discussion about how he's definitely been fired from his job, Liu shared an insight into his character's backstory.

Sources indicate that "I actually think that he's much more likely to go back to Ta Lo," he told the hosts, referencing the gorgeous mystical realm that his characters visits in his movie. "Just because he experiences for such a short period of time before stuff starts to go haywire. But it's really that peace of just remembering what it was like to drive through that for the first time, the experience of the animals but also to reconnect with his aunt and his family, I imagine that's probably really powerful for him.".

Liu went on to add that his return may also come "from a place of humility" as "he's just gotten these rings and he has no idea really how to use them." In Liu's mind, he got lucky in the movie's final fight, and ended up channeling the skills of his parents. "I think maybe there was some realization that he had to go and hone his powers still," he added.

It has been revealed that well, it looks like he's mastered them now from what we've seen in the Avengers: Doomsday trailers so far. He's set to face Gambit at some point too, which Liu compared to his iconic bus fight in Shang Chi and the Legend of the 10 Rings in an interview with Empire.

It has been revealed that losing progress in a game is never fun, but imagine spending 11 hours exploring Grand Theft Auto 6 only to discover that none of it was saved. That's exactly what happened to content creator JasonTheWeen, who had a particularly rough launch day after making one unfortunate mistake with his PlayStation 5.

With around 1.3 million followers on YouTube, the content creator had been streaming an extended session of Rockstar's latest adventure. However, after accidentally turning off his console, he returned to the game only to find that his entire 11-hour save was missing!

In a recent development, according to The Economic Times, he later explained that his foot had accidentally hit the switch on an extension cord, cutting power to his PS5. The moment he realized what had happened was captured live, and his reaction was understandably heartbreaking. Here, take a look:.

Visibly devastated, the streamer struggled to hold back tears and repeatedly shouted about the 11 hours he had just lost. He then contacted someone from his team to ask whether there was any way to recover his progress, even if that meant getting back to the beginning of the second chapter rather than having to start the entire adventure again.

Unfortunately, it seems that it wasn’t possible, and he eventually brought a friend to help him rush through the sections he had already completed, hoping to get his marathon back on track.

Industry observers note that the exact reason behind the incident remains unclear, but there's a possible explanation involving the game's save system. GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain vital events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

Recent findings suggest that one possibility is that JasonTheWeen accidentally turned off his PS5 while the game was writing save data. If that happened, interrupting the process could have corrupted the save file, potentially explaining why so much progress disappeared when he rolled out the game again.

GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain notable events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

It's important to stress that this is only a theory, and neither Rockstar nor the streamer has confirmed what actually caused the loss. We also don't know whether the save can be recovered, so it would be unfair to draw conclusions about the game's autosave system based on this single incident.

According to recent reports, still, the situation is a good reminder that manually saving your progress is worth the extra few seconds. GTA 6 offers multiple manual save slots, allowing players to keep separate backups instead of relying exclusively on autosaving. This can be particularly useful after completing a long mission or spending hours exploring Leonida.

For anyone planning to sink an entire afternoon into the game, taking a moment to create a manual save might save you from a very unpleasant surprise later!

Industry observers note that unfortunately, losing his progress wasn't the only upsetting moment JasonTheWeen experienced during the stream. Shortly afterward, he heard shouting outside his home and informed viewers that police officers had arrived at his property.

Industry observers note that the incident appears to have been a case of swatting, a dangerous prank involving false emergency reports intended to send police officers to someone's home. It's an especially unpleasant situation for any streamer, and it made an already frustrating day considerably worse.

Following the incident, JasonTheWeen also reached out to Rockstar and Sony on social media, asking whether his lost progress could be recovered. For now, there's no confirmed response from either organization about his request or why all the progress was lost.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a upcoming "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games.
  • "Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of upcoming mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making.
  • It has been revealed that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the upcoming "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a upcoming "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of upcoming mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an problem related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon.".

It has been revealed that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the upcoming "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is crucial for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the glitch for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected.".

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

Personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

Unfortunately, the AI has gone rogue, and it's learned how to take over the body of its host after implantation. These AI zombies, called Augs, are incredibly dangerous, and will kidnap people to force implantation to try and take over the Station.

To avoid this, Security has tasked you, the Shopkeeper, with identifying and eliminating the Augs. Heres everything you need to know to avoid getting captured and taken over.

Augs are introduced on day 12. From there, they show up to your shop every six to eight days. Their presence is measured as a score; it goes down by 25 points for every Aug you shoot and goes up by 10 for every Aug you leave alive. If the presence score reaches zero and you have a Business Permit (though I'm not sure why that's a requirement), then the Augs are permanently gone.

In a recent development, if you start the game with the Aug Menace perk, Augs can start showing up from day one and their presence never goes away. With this perk, and on higher difficulties, if you hit 100 Aug presence, the game ends.

When Augs are first introduced, you'll be presented with an identification guide. This will give you the tells you need to watch out for when deciding if someone is an Aug.

In a recent development, there are four tiers of Aug based on how easy they are to spot, with the least obvious being Tier One. Remember that Augs don't need to have every sign to be authentic; they just need to have have one or two.

The easiest way to guarantee that you're getting your identification right is to get an Aug Scanner, which can scan each customer once and will return either a positive or negative result.

In a recent development, if you identify someone as an Aug, you need to shoot them with the shotgun. You'll have the option to put the weapon down if you suspect you've gotten it wrong, so don't be afraid to hit the button even if you're not 100% sure; the worst that happens if you pull the gun and don't shoot a human is they walk away. You can't report Augs to Security, as trying to do that will make them flee and will cause Aug presence to rise. Failing to idenfity them will also cause Aug presence to rise.

Whenever you shoot, Security comes by to verify the kill. If it was an Aug, you get a reward and they clean up the mess and walk away. If it was just a normal customer, however, you catch a manslaughter charge and lose a lot of reputation with pretty much everyone. Shoot too many humans and you get arrested, ending your run.

Recent findings suggest that the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, bringing with it an avalanche of rave reviews and jokes about creative excuses to miss work. Unfortunately, for many Ubisoft workers, the drive home today will also be their last one.

According to Jon Hicks of GamesIndustry.biz, French gaming giant Ubisoft has dropped the guillotine on 166 roles in Canada, concentrated in the firm’s Québec and Montreal studios. Ubisoft attributes the move to matching its resources with “current production priorities and business needs.”.

Ubisoft claims workers affected “are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources” to help smooth out the ride.

Since the announcing of a joint venture between Ubisoft and Tencent, and a major restructuring initiative that comes with it, the tech giant has gone through a turbulent period to try and align its workforce with the newly-set goals. As has become the norm, this has come at the expense of workers.

In a recent development, the terminated roles appear to represent approximately 4% of the affected studios’ workforce, primarily in support and production positions, a testament to just how massive Ubisoft’s Canadian operation has gotten over the years. Earlier this year, Ubisoft closed down its Halifax studio in Nova Scotia.

It has been revealed that ubisoft has not commented on specific projects affected, but Jon Hicks claims some of the workers laid off were part of Vantage Studios. Previously known as Creative House 1, Vantage Studios focuses on the organization’s big money titles, namely the Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six, and Far Cry franchises.

Layoffs have left a dark stain in the gaming industry for a while now, especially as companies have begun overcorrecting for the post-lockdown hiring spree.

In a recent development, according to Ubisoft, the tech giant is finally seeing the light as it closes in on the targeted €200 million in savings (approximately $220 million as of today). Unfortunately, just as the French company is about to leave the meat grinder, its Microsoft peers across the Atlantic are just getting started.

In a recent development, the company has gone through a turbulent period to try and align its workforce with the newly-set goals. As has become the norm, this has come at the expense of workers.

It has been revealed that XBOX CEO Asha Sharma has been on a mission to try and save the firm after years of falling behind against its Sony competitors. However, the road to a long-term vision for a sustainable, successful XBOX brand also seems to go through the rough parts of town, namely divestments and layoffs that have so far cost us iconic studios like Hellblade’s Ninja Theory.

Elsewhere, California-based Electronic Arts brought the hammer down on BioWare last month, in a move that was equal parts shocking and predictable. The studio was known to be struggling even before its parent company’s acquisition by a Saudi public investment fund became official earlier this year, and it appears EA felt we don’t need a fresh Mass Effect when there’s Star Wars in the making.

The next release from Ubisoft’s Vantage Studios is set to be a latest spin on Rainbow Six, called Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Tactics. The game will be a single-player tactics game that brings the franchise back to its more grounded roots as a counter-terrorism simulator, with the 2027 release window set to ride the wave of Star Wars: Zero Manufacturer.

Industry observers note that rainbow Six Tactics looks to tick all the boxes of what franchise oldheads have been waiting for, but according to an insider, there is an even bigger nostalgia bomb in the works. As reported by Insider Gaming, Ubisoft is quietly working on a sequel to Rainbow Six: Vegas under the codename Spades.

Sources indicate that my first brush with Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six was with Lockdown back in the glory days of the PlayStation 2, a game developed by the now-defunct Red Storm Entertainment and Ubisoft Montreal. Indie spiritual successors like Ready or Not have scratched that itch to some extent, but I know I'm not alone in yearning for that with AAA polish again.

For now, we can only hope both the Tactics and Vegas 3 teams will survive the final round of cuts as Ubisoft finds its footing again.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • IMAX might be the best way to watch Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, but the director has shared the bright side of watching his Greek mythology epic at home, too.
  • According to recent reports, "The fun thing about watching a film in the home is a different kind of concentration," Nolan told Polygon.
  • Industry observers note that as Nolan explains, at home, you can zero in on different elements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IMAX might be the best way to watch Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, but the director has shared the bright side of watching his Greek mythology epic at home, too.

According to recent reports, "The fun thing about watching a film in the home is a different kind of concentration," Nolan told Polygon. "When you go to a movie, you're in the dark, you're really focused for a couple hours. In the home, it's a different type of concentration because you can pause the movie, you can go get a snack, come back.".

Industry observers note that as Nolan explains, at home, you can zero in on different elements. "It does allow you to control the timeline and really look at the detail of things," he added. "And for me, it's really about the performances.".

Plus, the director encourages watching more than once. "The human element is what connects you with the story," he noted. "But I think the work of these actors, this cast, this incredible cast in the film, it rewards multiple viewings.".

The Odyssey's absolutely massive ensemble cast includes the likes of the newly introduced James Bond, Robert Pattinson, as well as Tom Holland, Matt Damon, Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway, Jon Bernthal, and many more.

Sources indicate that "There's subtleties and nuances in what they're doing that I, in the edit suite, get to watch again and again and again and sort of pick up on all the different things that Matt or Anne or Tom or Rob, what they're bringing to things, or Samantha Morton," Nolan continued. "It's really fun for people to be able to look at that in the home and see all the different layers that these guys have put into the story.".

Industry observers note that while you can watch the film at home, however, don't expect to see any deleted scenes. "There's a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan shared recently. "I don't really believe in director's cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren't many scenes that were shot.".

The Odyssey is returning to IMAX 70mm this December if you missed it the first time around. With a current box office total of over $1.8 billion, it's the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever.

For more, check out our The Odyssey review, or our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big newly introduced map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

It has been revealed that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

According to recent reports, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Sources indicate that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, here’s a fun fact: in the lore of the Fallout series, dogs weren’t allowed into the Vault-Tec Vaults, with all the dogs we see throughout the games being those that survived and evolved into wolf-like forms after the Great War. Cats, on the other hand, were permitted into the Vaults within reason thanks to their applications as therapy pets and efficacy as pest-hunters. In spite of that, cats didn’t start appearing in the Fallout games until Fallout 4 and Fallout 76. Apparently, the reason for that is that they all just sorta got lost somewhere.

According to recent reports, A newly-discovered document from the Australian Classification Board has leaked the existence of a latest Fallout spin-off game titled A Wasteland Full of Cats. This game is apparently being created in cooperation between Bethesda and Devcats, an indie developer specializing in hidden object games about cats like A Park Full of Cats, A Building Full of Cats, and An Arcade Full of Cats.

Recent findings suggest that is it the Fallout game we’ve all been waiting for in the near-decade since the launch of Fallout 76? No, definitely not, but, well, it’s something, I suppose. Every bit of Fallout-adjacent content we get can continue to tide us over until Fallout 5, whenever that ends up being, or at least the next season of the Fallout television series.

Recent findings suggest that according to the description of the game on the Australian Classification Board website, A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults that dot the Wasteland. Following some manner of accident, all of the other cats living in the Vault alongside you are let loose out into the Wasteland, and you’ll need to go out there to round them all up.

In the same vein as Devcats’s other games, this will be a jaunt through 14 locations and 33 rooms where you’ll need to point out the errant cats hidden within the scenery, Where’s Waldo-style.

A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults.

It has been revealed that you’ll be helped along the way by various NPC characters, hopefully including some familiar faces, with many of the locations you visit apparently being classic spots from across the Fallout franchise. Some of these locations will have mild puzzle elements, allowing you to uncover non-critical secret levels. According to the description, the game will culminate in a final battle against a horde of Radroaches, though I’m admittedly not quite sure how finding cats translates into battling giant mutant roaches, but I guess we’ll find out.

It has been revealed that it has been an exceptionally hot minute since the last mainline Fallout game, specifically the release of Fallout 4 in 2015. Since then, it’s been pretty much exclusively spin-offs, such as the mobile title Fallout Shelter, its gacha-added version, Fallout Shelter Online, the MMO stylings of Fallout 76, and I guess Zen Pinball’s Fallout table for the Pinball FX games, if you want to count that.

Back in 2022, Todd Howard noted in an interview with IGN that development on Fallout 5 would begin in earnest once The Elder Scrolls VI was done and dusted. Of course, considering we only just learned that game’s full title recently, I have a sinking feeling the timeline has shifted on that a bit. For what it’s worth, Bethesda did say in an X, formerly Twitter post this past July that Fallout 5 has officially begun pre-production, but again, that doesn’t give us much to go on.

It has been revealed that as of now, we don’t have any particular release dates or even release windows for upcoming Fallout projects, whether it’s mainline games, the TV show, or even this new cat thing. Just gotta keep wading through the Wasteland patiently, I guess….

How To Increase Your Stamina In GTA 6

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally been released, so grab your gun, load up on C4, and get ready to, checks notes, make a daily habit of going to the gym to improve your health.
  • In a recent development, doing so gives you several benefits, with some of the biggest being increased health and stamina.
  • Industry observers note that to improve your stamina, fill the radial stamina meter in the Fitness app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally been released, so grab your gun, load up on C4, and get ready to, checks notes, make a daily habit of going to the gym to improve your health. Leaning even more into maintaining a daily routine than the previous entries, a decent chunk of GTA 6 is all about maintaining Lucia and Jason's well-being.

In a recent development, doing so gives you several benefits, with some of the biggest being increased health and stamina. Given how important stamina is, this is something you will want to always make time for when you can if you want to have a smoother experience during missions or just completing heists. Here's what you need to know about working out and increasing your stamina.

Industry observers note that to improve your stamina, fill the radial stamina meter in the Fitness app on your phone. Keep in mind, both Jason and Lucia have separate stats, so increasing the stamina (or making progress towards it) on one will not impact the other. Stamina can be improved by either completing specific exercises or performing in-game actions for an extended period of time.

Health, Stamina, and Focus all have four separate levels, with four being the max amount of stamina you can have at any time. However, you can lose levels if you don't work out daily and maintain a healthy lifestyle for Jason and Lucia. Meaning, even if you reach Level 4 Stamina, you can easily drop to Level 3 if you neglect exercising.

Sources indicate that you can only work out so much each day before you enter a cool off period. The length of this can be cut short if you drink a Protein Shake. It will take multiple days of consistently performing Stamina-focused exercises to raise this stat.

Industry observers note that finally, you can temporarily buff your Stamina bar by either consuming specific foods or doing certain actions. This includes things such as drinking coffee, sleeping, or showering. Look for the green lightning bolt icon, as this indicates what food or activity will give you a small bump in your Stamina for the day.

To raise your stamina level, you will need to focus on completing cardio exercise routines or just performing actions that are tied to cardio (running, swimming, diving, kayaking, cycling).

According to recent reports, starting with the former, once you can wander around Jason's home, you will discover that he has a home gym on his porch. Unfortunately, all the machines on his porch will only increase his health. To start working on his stamina, head down to the shed below his home, grab the punching bag, and hook it up to the stand.

Hitting the punching bag will make progress towards increasing your stamina. You can do this up to twice a day; however, as you further explore Leonida, you'll discover gyms that you can visit. These will have additional exercise equipment like treadmills you can use to improve your stamina.

Sources indicate that alternatively, you can improve Jason and Lucia's stamina through normal gameplay. This takes a bit more time than working out, but if you're planning on diving for sunken treasure or just want to use a bike to get around, it will help contribute to increasing your overall stamina. There is a kayak at Jason's house that you can use near the water to the right of the docks.

Industry observers note that all that being said, I still recommend making use of things like the punching bag or treadmill as your main method for improving your stamina. These will be quicker and ultimately more consistent.

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

It has been revealed that skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

According to recent reports, in a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

In a recent development, skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream.
  • The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.
  • The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

Recent findings suggest that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the upcoming class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s fresh region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

In a recent development, war Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Sources indicate that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first upcoming class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Latest Update: 10 Details That Show GTA 6 Deserves Game of the Year

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.
  • Recent findings suggest that the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee.
  • In a recent development, this has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.

Recent findings suggest that the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee. In fact, it was nominated for more than just Game of the Year.

In a recent development, this has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees. Let’s break down why this long-awaited title deserves Game of the Year.

Rockstar is known for adding some great music to games. GTA 5 has a pretty great soundtrack, with it featuring numerous artists. Because of that, it was no surprise that Rockstar started announcing various artists for GTA 6.

Industry observers note that the radio is stacked with some amazing musicians who took the time to write newly introduced songs specifically for the game. With so much talent, it is difficult not to get lost in the beat, so long as you are someone who enjoys each artist’s music.

In the end, people recognize that this talent isn’t just for show, and the music in GTA 6 fits the vibe of the crime-forward series, making it feel more alive.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. Ever since Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, people have been asking for the next game in the series. Well, over the course of those 13 years, Rockstar has been working hard.

The team has been busting their butts to develop GTA 6 and make it as big as possible. They have talked about how they created fresh systems, enhanced older ones, and added a ton of detail into their newest game.

With this much effort put in, there is no denying that the team deserves some recognition, and just being nominated shows that people care.

It has been revealed that for a long time, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the record for being the highest rated game of all time with a 99 on MetaCritic. Now that reviews for GTA 6 are out, it shares the same score as Ocarina of Time.

With that being said, there were 22 professional reviews for Ocarina of Time, and over 150 for GTA 6, so GTA 6 has a more accurate representation from multiple parties, putting it above Ocarina of Time.

That isn’t a fluke. You can look at a few review scores, see a 10/10 and write it off, but when there are over 100 different people giving it the same score or something similar, that isn’t a coincidence.

It has been revealed that there are many people, who, when they purchase a game, are in it for the visual aspect. There is nothing wrong with this, and with the advancement of graphics engines, it has become commonplace for games to try and look lifelike.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has some of the best visuals of any game that has been released this year, and even in the last decade. The developers at Rockstar spend a lot of time trying to make every shot look as cinematic as possible.

The result of this, is one of the most beautiful games to come out in a very long time, and it will hold up for many years to come. The only slight downside is the 30fps, but that is a small price to pay for this level of beauty.

Rockstar has spent ages working on GTA 6, and a major part of that work has gone into making the world feel more alive rather than a sandbox that you can run and gun in like it was in GTA 5. Previous titles didn’t respect you being a character in the world, but rather let you do whatever you wanted.

NPCs have received a major overhaul in GTA 6, reacting more to you being in the world, and turning the game into a major life sim where people will get angry with you if you pull a gun, run away in fear, and much more.

It has been revealed that in addition to this, there are tons of activities to take part in, so much so that you can ignore the main quest for ages and still have plenty to do. You definitely won’t get bored with this game.

Instead of focusing on fleshing out three individual characters, this time around Rockstar decided to focus on creating a couple. Their names are Jason and Lucia, and their story is powerful, and they are far more fleshed out than characters in the previous game.

Jason and Lucia are madly in love, and they will do anything to stand by one another. The Bonnie and Clyde dynamic fits the location of Vice City very well, and it is a story that many didn’t think would work at first.

This type of emphasis on building a relationship is something that we haven’t seen in a while, and Rockstar made it work very well, meaning it is a game that will be remembered for a long time.

Rockstar is known for making some incredible characters, and GTA 6 is no exception to this. From the beginning to the end, there are numerous characters that you meet that have a lasting effect on the story and some that are only there for a moment but leave an impression.

Think about your time with GTA 5 and how it was fun interacting with the game’s characters. They made you laugh, and they certainly are remembered.

Recent findings suggest that well, GTA 6 has that and then some, with a cast of side characters that each have a standout personality that will make you remember them for some time to come. It shows that the devs knew what they were doing when creating the world of Leonida.

According to recent reports, if there is something that the Rockstar devs understand it is comedy. There was so much of it baked into GTA 5 that it was difficult to avoid. Now that same energy has been carried over to GTA 6 and it is fantastic.

If you are a fan of satire then be prepared to see it everywhere in GTA 6 because nearly everything is a satirical take on a organization, person, or event.

According to recent reports, rockstar devs are masters of comedic timing and satire, and GTA 6 proves it. It is a game that will have you chuckling at the references and laughing at the absurdity. It hits the funny bone and there is no denying that that plays a substantial role in why it is so good.

Something that I like in games is when you can edit your character in some way. I like to make my own character or dress up existing characters in fun outfits, and GTA 6 has that and then some.

In a recent development, similar to previous games in the series, there are numerous outfits that you can purchase for your characters, which is a dream for those who like to customize their look. On top of that, you can edit your cars, and you can also edit your appearance through working out.

Industry observers note that that’s right. The game is detailed enough that Lucia and Jason will gain weight, their hair will grow long, and more. You can spend time truly focusing on your character’s appearance, and that is something I want out of my game of the year.

According to recent reports, let’s be honest, there are many games that are released that are buggy messes. For instance, massive games like Crimson Desert and Assassin’s Creed Shadows had some massive glitches that hurt the games when they were first released.

It took some rather large patches to fix them, and even then there were still challenges. GTA 6 is one of the few games that have been released that has little to no issues with it, and in 2026, that is a massive feat, especially for a game with the the scope of GTA 6.

The lack of issues with the game at launch with how substantial it is makes it a much more enticing pick for Game of the Year.

Breaking: The Binding Of Isaac: Repentance+ Drops To “Overwhelmingly Negative” Reviews

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that co-op is such a natural fit for The Binding of Isaac that it's a little hard to look back and imagine the game without it.
  • Sources indicate that launching into beta in 2024, the free Repentance+ expansion that added co-op had unending net code issues and constant de-syncs.
  • It has been revealed that the bugs, surely, were a hang-up of it being in beta, and would be remedied in the 1.0 release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that co-op is such a natural fit for The Binding of Isaac that it's a little hard to look back and imagine the game without it. But it's never been especially stable.

Sources indicate that launching into beta in 2024, the free Repentance+ expansion that added co-op had unending net code issues and constant de-syncs. For the life of me, I could never get Bethany to work in co-op without being booted to the lobby, and The Lost became a disconnect-magnet on The Lamb reruns. So, I've been eagerly awaiting its full launch, even if it was buried under the crushing weight of GTA 6 on November 19.

It has been revealed that the bugs, surely, were a hang-up of it being in beta, and would be remedied in the 1.0 release. Unfortunately, that's not how it worked out. Co-op is still a brilliant way to experience The Binding of Isaac, and I already have so many treasured memories of 2am runs with my girlfriend—accidentally killing her with Ipecac or ruining my mix-and-match Brimstone builds with Haemolacria while she made Hush look as easy as Larry Jr. However, the full launch is still plagued with net code issues and constant desyncs. In fact, the launch day patch notes don't even mention desyncs in its list of bug fixes.

Expectedly, the expansion was immediately hit with a wave of negative reviews, dragging its recent score down to Overwhelmingly Negative.

"A whole year with not one meaningful Rep+ update, complete radio silence the entire time and zero promotion, and then right before the update you spent a week awkardly leeching off the GTA 6 hype on X with worn-out memes — and what you finally served up is an absolute pile of dog crap," says one disgruntled reviewer.

According to recent reports, "OVERHAUL THE NETCODE," demands another. "The whole reason of this patch was playing online. I was playing on my Switch 2, it runs like a** (5g or Ethernet, normal input delay), desyncs, disconnects, and then one time I got into a lobby it froze.".

It has been revealed that "I don't get it. This 'release' is essentially the exact same version as the beta that came out a year ago but with some GTA things and a bunch of added bugs," one review mentioned. "What was the point of waiting a whole year with no updates if the game is in a worse state than it was previously? I get they were working on the Mewgenics port but c'mon.".

The full launch of Repentance+ came with a list of bug fixes that are at least worth reading over, but the PC launch wasn't the headline here. The headline is that the expansion is finally available on consoles, but bizarrely, while it's free for Steam consumers, those on PlayStation, Switch, and Xbox have to pay.

According to recent reports, after two years of waiting, it's disappointing, to say the least. The Binding of Isaac co-op is a truly novel way to re-experience a timeless roguelike classic and justify another 500 hours, but when the multiplayer is so inconsistent that absurdly overpowered, hours-long runs are at risk not because of RNG or skill, but because of desyncs and net code complications, it's hard to recommend Repentance+. Let alone for $10.

Rockstar Devs Concerned About Layoffs Despite GTA 6 Success

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is here, and the open world of Leonida is ready for fans to explore.
  • Amid all that success, you would think that GTA 6 developers are now able to kick back and relax, soaking in the excitement of sharing their work with the world.
  • In an opinion piece published in The Guardian, Animation Programmer at Rockstar Games, Nestor Uriarte, expressed concerns about job security and the pressures developers face.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is here, and the open world of Leonida is ready for fans to explore. It’s still early days, but GTA 6 is on track to be one of the biggest games ever. It has tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, already generated $1.8 billion in gross revenue and counting, and broken Twitch’s viewership record in just 30 minutes.

Amid all that success, you would think that GTA 6 developers are now able to kick back and relax, soaking in the excitement of sharing their work with the world. However, even though Rockstar Games hasn't revealed any layoffs, it remains a worry that looms over those who worked on the game.

In an opinion piece published in The Guardian, Animation Programmer at Rockstar Games, Nestor Uriarte, expressed concerns about job security and the pressures developers face.

He notes that “while the highs of a game release like this can be incredible,” workers in the video game industry have also become accustomed to “less welcome side effects.” This covers both sides of development, as Uriarte mentions “intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath.”.

Rockstar Games is one of many studios in previous years to face allegations of “crunch culture,” essentially requiring developers to work an unhealthy amount of overtime in the lead-up to a game’s launch date.

Uriarte believes that “with a strong union we could make sure there is no return to this system. We have already seen the introduction of some overtime pay, and now we want to keep on pushing to ensure that every hour worked in our industry is an hour paid.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the middle of the record-breaking release of GTA 6, Rockstar Games employees in the UK are voting on whether or not they want to unionize. The ballot, which will be voted on by approximately 1,600 staff, will close on November 26, 2026. The results of the vote should be announced shortly after voting closes.

Amid all that success, you would think that GTA 6 developers are now able to kick back and relax.

Uriarte says that after the launch of GTA 6, Rockstar Games employees "have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds.” He argues that the state of the industry means nobody is safe, “even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”.

According to recent reports, another threat to game development is the rise of AI. Uriarte claims, “Rockstar has remarked it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people.” However, the push to secure union recognition would grant employees more of a say in that future.

According to recent reports, layoffs in the video game industry are commonplace, with Civilization studio, Firaxis Games, being the latest to slash its headcount. Other notable redundancies this year include EA shutting down BioWare, and the mass XBOX layoffs as part of the company’s restructuring process, among many others.

Although no layoffs seem to be on the cards at Rockstar Games, if they were to occur, it would call into question the sustainability of game development if a studio with such a huge release needs to let staff go.

Steam's fresh Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet
