⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck.
  • The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide.
  • According to recent reports, or will you?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

According to recent reports, or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

It has been revealed that there's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

Sources indicate that as for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot new enhancement that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest upgrade, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for patch 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an glitch that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into complications with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s revision takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an problem that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

In a recent development, finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you miss the days of unfolding a paper map before heading into a latest GTA game, Rockstar has something for you. The official map of Leonida is now available to download for free, and there's a print-ready version for anyone who wants a physical copy.

Sources indicate that rockstar added the map to its GTA 6 website on November 19, the same day the game rolled out. You can also download the game's cover art as a poster, so there are actually two things worth grabbing if you've got a printer handy.

According to recent reports, head to the official GTA 6 media page and look for the section labeled 'Leonida Map & Cover Art Poster.' Select 'View Options' to open the downloads. Rockstar has separate choices for the Leonida map and cover art, including printable versions of both.

In a recent development, pick 'Leonida Map - Printable' if you want to put it on paper, then use the download button. There's a regular map download as well, which is handy if you just want to keep a copy on your phone, tablet, or second monitor while you play.

According to recent reports, the map gives you a proper look at the shape of Leonida, from Vice City's dense roads to the waterways, coastlines, and smaller areas further inland. If you've spent the last few years comparing trailer shots and fan-made maps, being able to look at Rockstar's official version is a pretty nice change.

According to recent reports, if you want the entire thing rather than a cropped section, choose a matching paper size or ask a print shop to scale it to fit. The print-ready download is the version to use for that.

The other download is the game's cover art poster. Rockstar has made it available in a print-ready format too, so you can hang it up instead of just using it as a desktop wallpaper.

In a recent development, there's a bit of GTA history behind the appeal. Physical copies of GTA 3, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5 all came with paper maps. Even spin-offs like Liberty City Stories, Vice City Stories, and Episodes from Liberty City followed that tradition. You could spend ages looking over the streets and place names before you'd actually explored them in-game.

Sources indicate that I've lost the map that came with my copy of GTA: Episodes from Liberty City, and I'm sure some of you have misplaced yours too. Even the maps we've managed to keep aren't necessarily in great shape. Leaving them folded inside a game case for years can damage the paper along the creases. Having an official file you can print again is a pretty good solution to that.

You can obviously save the new map and check it on another screen, but printing it is half the appeal. Having something physical to look at while you explore Leonida feels a lot closer to those older releases.

You can obviously save the new map and check it on another screen, but printing it is half the appeal.

It has been revealed that I can already see the Leonida map and GTA 6 cover art decorating plenty of fans' rooms. I'd be surprised if a fair few people didn't end up printing both.

Sources indicate that if you'd rather have a professionally printed copy, Rockstar has another option coming. In its November 3 announcement, the company mentioned a double-sided physical poster would be sold through the Rockstar Store shortly after launch.

Sources indicate that that version will cost $0.99 on its own, or come free with another Rockstar Store purchase. Rockstar hasn't given an exact date for when it will go on sale, though, so don't confuse that upcoming physical item with the digital files you can download right now.

Boxed copies of GTA 6 are available, but as DualShockers previously reported, they contain download codes rather than discs. Reports on the PS5 edition also confirm that the case includes an artwork poster, not the traditional fold-out map. Whether Rockstar will ever bundle a map with a later boxed release is still unclear.

Sources indicate that it would've been even better if Rockstar had confirmed that a physical Leonida map would come with the game, like it did with the older releases. Still, making high-resolution printable versions of both the map and cover art available for free is a good move. And unlike an old folded map, you can always print a fresh copy if yours gets damaged.

There's something nice about having an official paper map beside you while playing GTA, and now anyone who wants one can print it without having to track down a boxed copy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is without a doubt already proving successful, sitting as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic – but this quick success and its massive earning estimates aren't enough to curb fears of further layoffs at Rockstar Games.
  • The developers have spoken out about these concerns, with animation programmer Nestor Uriarte admitting he's "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time" – you know, Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Industry observers note that clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has something to say on the matter, too, sharing her thoughts over on Instagram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is without a doubt already proving successful, sitting as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic – but this quick success and its massive earning estimates aren't enough to curb fears of further layoffs at Rockstar Games.

The developers have spoken out about these concerns, with animation programmer Nestor Uriarte admitting he's "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time" – you know, Grand Theft Auto 6. Finance experts like Square Enix veteran Jacob Novak also stated the game's success indeed isn't enough to stop layoffs, as Rockstar has "built the biggest, most expensive game of all time and now released it.".

Industry observers note that clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has something to say on the matter, too, sharing her thoughts over on Instagram. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation," she writes. "Yet the team is worried about layoffs. So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor?".

According to recent reports, sadly, as Svedberg-Yen describes, "Not the vast majority of the creative team. One of the issues that happens when people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value. In finance, we call that value extraction." With this effect in mind – one I'd argue we've unfortunately seen a good bit of over the past few years within the video game industry – she hopes that Rockstar can successfully unionize."I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," the writer concludes. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." While that's certainly true, it's unfortunately not always the reality – and that's precisely why Svedberg-Yen is rooting for unionization.

It has been revealed that just a day or so ago, she detailed how the industry "is eating itself" amid layoffs and studio closures, saying, "A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart." It's hard to not let it break your heart, honestly, as, again, it's not just Rockstar. We've reported on layoffs across various companies over recent years, ranging from Microsoft's aims to cut 3,200 employees at Xbox to BioWare's closure following the EA buyout.

Here's hoping that everyone lands on their feet at the end of it all – and that studios take notes from the likes of Nintendo's late president Satoru Iwata, who wisely said "employees who fear that they may be laid off" will never produce the same results as those who don't.

Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

It has been revealed that the major new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

It has been revealed that varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Industry observers note that varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

It has been revealed that the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

It has been revealed that staying on the theme of reminiscence, the massive event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

According to recent reports, outside of events, there’s a newly introduced set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

GTA 6: How to Steal the Red Phoenix

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 keeps the actual mandatory crimes very grounded during its opening hours, far from the previous series openings of massive police shootouts and gang wars bursting at the seams.
  • To secure some product left behind by an arrested junkie, Brian tasks Jason with securing a red Phoenix, a sleazy sports car with too much weed in the trunk to just walk away with.
  • In a recent development, before you can yoink the car, you’ll need to start its mission, ‘Unwanted Attention’, by meeting with Cal at one of his fishing spots in Corsair Key.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 keeps the actual mandatory crimes very grounded during its opening hours, far from the previous series openings of massive police shootouts and gang wars bursting at the seams. One of the very first jobs Jason is tasked with sounds fairly simple, but is shockingly involved.

To secure some product left behind by an arrested junkie, Brian tasks Jason with securing a red Phoenix, a sleazy sports car with too much weed in the trunk to just walk away with. Getting it out of the police impound is easier said than done, so let’s go over it step by step.

In a recent development, before you can yoink the car, you’ll need to start its mission, ‘Unwanted Attention’, by meeting with Cal at one of his fishing spots in Corsair Key. Mark his location via your text messages and drive to the northeast down the highway. These roads are tight, so be careful when trying to pull past other drivers.

Once you’ve snagged Cal, he’ll explain the job, marking the police impound where the Phoenix is at the moment being held. Once you arrive, you can choose between charging straight in with your newly acquired gear, or sneaking around the side through a hole in the barbed wire fence surrounding the other walls.

Stealthing through the impound is much simpler, with very few guards on patrol. If you’re looking to keep your Criminal Profile at a Professional level, hug the left side of the impound’s outer wall until you see an opening in the barbed wire, giving you an opportunity to hop in.

Now that you’re inside the impound itself, you’ll need to sneak past the two patrolling guards. One is wandering around the gate itself, while the other is deeper inside, near the red Phoenix. You’ll be prompted to use the Waink It app to help you identify the ride, but it always spawns in the northeast end of the impound, still hooked up to a winch.

Industry observers note that the guards’ patrol patterns don’t overlap, so feel free to wander past or choke them out at your own discretion. Remember, nonlethal takedowns are easy ways to pivot your Criminal Profile towards Professional, or you can finish them off if you’re feeling a bit crueler.

Once you find the red Phoenix, don’t hop in immediately. Instead, enter the building behind it to find the guard manning the gate itself. Silently take him down, then hit a button on the wall to open the gate. Once the gate is open, lower the winch the Phoenix is attached to and hotwire it.

Now it’s time to bail! Drive straight through the open gate, and you’ll become Wanted, but since all the local cops are either unconscious or checking on their unresponsive allies, you’ve got a window before they arrive. Stick to backstreets or off-road routes to lose the cops quick.

In a recent development, once you’re all clear, head back over to Hamlet and visit the marked Spray N’ Pray shop to change the car’s paint job. Any will do the trick, even if losing the Phoenix decal is a shame. Once you do, you’ll be able to drop it off at Brian’s Garage for your reward, just enough to buy a new outfit to get off the radar completely.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has unveiled that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

According to recent reports, as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

Industry observers note that on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still reveals that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Sources indicate that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

This announcement was shared this week during The MIX Fall Showcase, with Stairway Games and Balor Games officially confirming a Switch 2 version will release alongside the free "Kids Grow Up" 1.4 Revision in winter 2026.

In this title, inspired by games such as Stardew Valley, you'll be able to experience a "cozy coastal life" either solo or with up to four friends in multiplayer.

Along the way, players can cultivate Starlet Town, protect local landscapes, dive beneath the waves to explore the magical Merfolk Kingdom, and even find love and build a family.

It has been revealed that the 1.4 “Kids Grow Up” Update opens a fresh chapter for Coral Island. Players who choose to embrace parenthood can experience new milestones together as a family as their children grow and develop hobbies and interests of their own. The neighborhood kids are getting older, too, bringing exciting new stories and interactions to Starlet Town.

Farm. Decorate. Craft. Explore. Relax. Players shape their own future—and the future of Coral Island.

So, if this looks like a cosy farming sim you might be interested in, be on the lookout for its arrival on the Switch 2 soon.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 rolls out with two editions, including the $100 Ultimate Edition that has a range of exclusive goodies, including shops, clothes, vehicles, and more.
  • As Rockstar detailed back when the Ultimate Edition was first revealed, the deluxe version's unique items aren't all available from the very start of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for some time, everyone feared that Grand Theft Auto 6 would cost $100 and raise the bar for triple-A prices going forward. As we know now, that's mostly not the case.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 rolls out with two editions, including the $100 Ultimate Edition that has a range of exclusive goodies, including shops, clothes, vehicles, and more. The way they work is a little strange, though.

As Rockstar detailed back when the Ultimate Edition was first revealed, the deluxe version's unique items aren't all available from the very start of the game. Although a few, like the Electric Fang Tattoo Parlour and Goodtime Gear, can be accessed from the start of the game, the more interesting bonuses are spaced out a bit.

Industry observers note that for example, the Hawk & Little Morgan Revolvers are only available once you reach Chapter 2, while the stunning ’95 Grotti Cheetah isn't available until all the way in Chapter 5. The shops offering exclusive cosmetics like tattoos and hairstyles can be accessed from the start, but some don't offer their unique styles until Chapter 2.

In a recent development, to make things a little easier, GTA 6 does at least tell you when you've gained access to some of the Ultimate Edition's items, either by adding a collection mission to the menu or showing a pop-up during gameplay. For almost all of them, though, they become available at the start of a chapter - it just changes for each item. Here's when and where to expect them.

Jason's safehouse in the Keys (only for Chapter 1).

Chapter 1 for Jason, Chapter 2 for Lucia.

Look in the weapon locker of any Ammu-Nation.

Wonder Whale, Key Lento, found on mannequins.

North Leonard County, above Lake Leonida.

Visit South Vice-Dale County first, robberies then appear in Southside.

Chapter 1, but Signature styles unlock from Chapter 2.

Collected from your Paradise Garage.

New sidequest is started once you collect the '67 Dominator Buggy.

Look in the weapon locker of any Ammu-Nation.

Head to the Ocean View Hotel in Vice Beach to unlock the new clothes, garage, and hairstyles.

Collected from Washington Beach, Vice Beach.

Added to various stores a few missions into the chapter.

Pegassi Residences parking garage.

It has been revealed that I wasn't able to test this myself, but various Grand Theft Auto 6 players have shown what happens to the various shops and locations if you don't have the Ultimate Edition. They don't disappear from the map like some expected, but Jason and Lucia simply won't be able to access them since the doors will be locked.

If that bothers you, there's an Ultimate Edition upgrade that can be purchased at any time. I personally think the extra $20 is worth it, but it really depends on how much you're going to be customising Jason and Lucia, since it's mostly just cosmetic options.

Lego big figures are at their best when depicting robots, if you ask me; they capture that sharp and angular look perfectly, and they don't step into the uncanny valley. According to recent reports, as of now, you can get it for $83.99 at Amazon (down from $140) in the 2026 Lego Black Friday deals. That's the cheapest it's ever been, and thanks to a Black Friday deal badge, I doubt it'll be available for less any time soon.

Based in the UK? The same set is £95.99 at Amazon instead of £120. That particular offer isn't a record low, but it is significantly better than the usual £117 or so it normally sits at.

There are plenty of Christmas-themed Black Friday Lego deals if you want them to get holly and jolly; I've seen multiple kits hit either record low prices or a very decent discount.

It has been revealed that as an example, the Lego Upscaled Santa Minifigure has never been cheaper than its current $41.99 at Amazon rather than $60 (or £40.99 at Amazon instead of £55 if you're based in the UK). Similarly, the Snowmen Ornaments are $10.99 via Amazon right now, down from $12.99.

If you're stuck for ideas on what to get your folks or spouse that are fun yet also high quality, I'd always recommend the Lego Botanicals range. They're usually of an impressively high quality and span a host of styles from bouquets to pot plants, so you can pick whatever you think they'd like best.

A huge host of these are on offer via Amazon US, so if you want to pick some up and get your Christmas shopping done early, now's the time.

I mentioned this discount yesterday while covering this year's Lego Black Friday deals, and it's worth revisiting because it's so darn good.

Second, it's got an impressive price cut. US fans are looking at 15% off via Amazon, while UK builders can pick up the set for £43.99 at Amazon rather than the usual £55.

Industry observers note that one of the most highly anticipated sets of the year, Minas Tirith, has hit its first price cut in the UK as part of this year's Black Friday Lego deals. In terms of sheer spectacle, I'd say this is the most impressive Lego set of the entire year. Besides being absolutely massive enough to draw every eye in a room, it cleverly uses forced perspective (e.g. it gets smaller as it goes up) and multiple scales to really sell the idea of how massive this Lord of the Rings city is. Sources indicate that while every store is trying to get in on the Black Friday sale, I'd argue that a couple are rising above the pack. From my experience scouring the shelves, some are sporting a lot more eyecatching discounts than others.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of newly introduced content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one upgrade on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s newly introduced blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

Recent findings suggest that the first stage of the fresh roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

It has been revealed that the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

Recent findings suggest that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers complications around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more complications join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next revision will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported problems.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies.".

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers.".

In a recent development, their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote.".

It has been revealed that solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6. This doesn’t mean that we didn’t have some good times with GTA 5, but all good things must eventually come to an end.

Industry observers note that now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes. Some of the best memories for people were made with that game. Communities came together, lawsuits were filed, and more.

GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.

In a recent development, there are multiple memes that were spawned thanks to GTA 5. For instance, Trevor kidnapping a guy’s wife will always live rent free in my head, but one of the biggest was the “Davey, how you doing,” meme.

Industry observers note that the scene is simple; Michael just meets up with Davey at the observatory. Well, this sparked a massive collection of memes, and it was mostly thanks to the ability to initiate the cutscene in different ways.

It has been revealed that people started reenacting the cutscene in real life, and doing absurd things in game like crashing a blimp into the observatory to initiate the cutscene. It will forever remain in people’s minds.

According to recent reports, while yes, GTA 6 is now here, that doesn’t mean that GTA 5 is gone. While people may be leaving the story behind, the online mode still exists, and it is still one of the most popular online games that exist.

It is estimated that there are around 8.5 to 10 million active users in GTA Online each week, and they aren’t going to just abandon the online because of GTA 6, at least not while there isn’t a upcoming GTA Online to flock to.

In a recent development, GTA 5 will continue to live on through the online mode for the next year until the next iteration of GTA Online is released. At that point, I may have to write another article.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 5 is the first and only game in the GTA series to have three protagonists: Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. Many people were concerned about there being three protagonists because it might dilute each character.

In a recent development, to everyone’s surprise, it didn’t dilute any of the characters, and it instead enhanced them. The characters work off each other, and it helped build the narrative.

Despite it being 13 years, there are people who still remember quotes from the game. People can describe full scenes and story beats. It is pretty amazing. That type of dedication never goes away. It’s similar to the adults who can still quote early episodes of SpongeBob.

Can we take a moment to reflect on how many copies of GTA 5 were sold worldwide? The game sold approximately 235 million copies within the last 13 years. This is one of the most sold games in the history of gaming.

That type of legacy doesn’t just go away. Only a few games have sold more copies than GTA 5, and they include Minecraft and Tetris. That is a very impressive feat.

Up until this year, kids have begged their parents to purchase them GTA 5, and adults have caved in to see what the hype was all about. With it being as big as it was, GTA 5 will never be forgotten. It will go down in gaming history and that is a fact.

It has been revealed that GTA 5 isn’t going to be forgotten anytime soon, and if you want proof, look at the current sales. I don’t mean the sales numbers over the last 13 years, I mean the sales numbers from the last week or so.

Within the last quarter, it is estimated that Rockstar sold another 5 million copies of GTA 5. That is ridiculous when you consider that the game is 13 years old.

The hype around GTA 6 has been increasing sales for past GTA titles, but it has mostly had the effect of increasing the sales number of GTA 5, which means that people will still be playing the story for the next year while they wait for GTA Online 2.0 to be released.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 5 was released during a time when people still got together to play games. While the main focus is connecting with people online, there are many who got together during the time of GTA 5 and played the game together in the same room.

Recent findings suggest that parties were formed, and people played the game together. They formed a bond, and that bond carried over into GTA Online, where people continued to play together and make memories.

These memories are still with those who played the game together and continue to enjoy the online. I played online with multiple friends and I will forever remember those times we shared before the next evolution of the online is released.

Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series is record-breaking, and there is no doubt about that. GTA 5 alone broke multiple records, and that is something that people won’t forget.

As far as records go, GTA 5 broke the record for highest-24 hour entertainment revenue, best-selling video game in 24 hours, best-selling action-adventure game in 24 hours, highest grossing video game in 24 hours, fastest game to reach $1billion in revenue, and more.

Recent findings suggest that when the game released, it was a huge deal, and it reveals through the number of copies that were sold, and it shows even more through the number of records that were broken by it. In total, it broke at least eight records. I can’t think of another game that has done that, and now it is GTA 6’s turn.

Industry observers note that whenever a massive game comes out that parodies stuff in real life, it is bound to attract a few lawsuits, and boy was GTA 5 the center of quite a few lawsuits over the years. One of the earlier ones was from Daz Dillinger who issued a cease and desist letter.

After that, other celebrities like Lindsay Lohan and Karen Gravano filed lawsuits against Rockstar over GTA 5, with one being over an alleged likeness and the other being about a character who mirrored their life.

Sources indicate that there was even once a lawsuit over GTA Online because it didn’t launch with the release of the game and was instead released some time later. While it isn’t the best look, this attention still attracts people to the game and it makes people remember the name.

In a recent development, do you believe that violent video games make people more violent in real life? Many don’t believe so, but there is a sect of those who think there is a link between violent behavior and video games, especially when the game has carjackings, murder, and other criminal activities.

In 2021, GTA V was mentioned in law HB3531 filed in Illinois. The goal of this law was to prohibit the sale of games featuring “psychological harm.” Ultimately, it wanted to restrict the sale of games like GTA 5 that featured criminal activity, meaning GTA 5 would get banned.

This wasn’t the first time the series came under fire from lawmakers, and it probably won’t be the last, but it leaves a lasting impression that people still remember and will help GTA 5 live on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

Sources indicate that hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

Recent findings suggest that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Recent findings suggest that aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

Industry observers note that the Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

Sources indicate that that stated, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

In a recent development, the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

Recent findings suggest that the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director says it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just rapidly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

November is a huge month for video games, with not only the release of the Ocarina of Time remake but also the long-awaited (and highly anticipated) arrival of GTA 6 this week.

In a recent development, while most games decided to avoid this month, one other title that has been released over the past week is TANUKI: Pon's Summer. If you are wondering why a game starring a BMX-riding tanuki decided to go up against these two juggernauts, it seems the Zelda news caught it by surprise.

Although it was prepared for GTA 6's arrival, Nintendo only announced the release of Ocarina's remake in September, and then introduced it at the start of November. Here's what Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards had to say about this during an interview with Games Industry:.

"While we originally decided on October to launch, due to marketing opportunities with first-party platforms, we decided that the sweet spot would be just clear of GTA 6's initial launch period. What I don't think we could have accounted for was Nintendo shadow-dropping the release of Ocarina of Time [on November 5].".

According to recent reports, he further notes how there's "probably a fair bit more of an overlap with "Switch 2 Zelda players" for Tanuki than there would be for GTA 6". Despite this, there's hope the title can still find "long-term" success through "word-of-mouth" style marketing, and that maybe some players will pick up the "BMXing Tanuki game" once they're done with Nintendo and Rockstar's games.

We gave Tanuki: Pon's Summer seven out of ten stars in our NL review, describing it as a cosy game you can get lost in.

Recent findings suggest that will you be making time for this game at some point? Are you planning to check out any other smaller titles during this busy time of year? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.

It has been revealed that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and quickly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. As such, millions of people were waiting at midnight on November 19, when the game became available in their region.

Industry observers note that or not. It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early. This is thanks to a trick that’s much easier to pull off on XBOX than PlayStation 5, prompting lots of people to change their nationality.

According to recent reports, A report by Ampere Analysis (with thanks to Eurogamer) has revealed that over two million XBOX players used the “Fresh Zealand trick” to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early. 100,000 PlayStation 5 users did something similar, but that method was more difficult, which is why the number is much smaller.

In a recent development, the Latest Zealand trick has been used for many big releases on XBOX systems in the past. Because of time zone differences, most video games launch in New Zealand first. If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Sources indicate that the PlayStation 5 version of the trick involves creating a separate account with billing information, which is a massive pain in the neck, which explains why only 100,000 people bothered. The Latest Zealand XBOX trick literally takes a minute to pull off and is easy to revert afterward.

If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Sources indicate that some fans were concerned that Microsoft would ban accounts that did the Fresh Zealand trick. After all, it breaks the Microsoft Store's terms of service. However, many official XBOX social media accounts playfully encouraged people to do it, as it was essentially a free win for the brand, at a time when it badly needed one. As it stands, there are reports of bans, even now that the trick isn’t necessary, so there's no need for anyone to worry about switching flags.

According to recent reports, while the Newly introduced Zealand trick is well-known among fans, and is something many gaming outlets will gleefully inform the public about ahead of a big release, it’s usually only done by a small audience. Grand Theft Auto 6 is such a massive game that more people than usual temporarily became Kiwis, giving them an early chance to play.

Industry observers note that now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, it’s unclear what the next big game will have a similar effect. 2027 has some massive hits, but it would be hard to claim any will be as important as Grand Theft Auto VI. If Persona 6 manages to launch in 2027, then the JRPG audience on XBOX might all take a journey to Mordor, but it’ll be unlikely that millions will do so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the #SaveMassEffect petition has rallied over 300,000 signatures, urging EA to resume development on Mass Effect: Universe with "sufficient funding, staffing, and time"—failing that, it called on the publisher to sell or license the IP to another studio. EA has not responded to the petition or the calls on social media for the series to continue, so, aside from the upcoming Prime Video series, the future of Mass Effect is in limbo. However, Commander Shepard herself has an idea on how to get the Normandy and its crew back on course.

In an interview with GamesRadar+, Jennifer Hale mentioned she was actually "excited and hopeful" when BioWare shut down, because she has "this vision of all these fans coming together, making a glorious Kickstarter, just like the folks at Critical Role did.".

Her idea, plainly, is that instead of just petitioning to Save Mass effect, fans should pool together the funds to buy the IP from EA outright. "One of those kind of Kickstarters," she mentioned. "Games are expensive, so maybe one or two well-heeled individuals who enjoy investing in creative ventures come along and fortify that. Then an indie game company, or any game company with openness and vision that's story-driven and community-conscious, comes into the picture to make it so.".

Hale states that the group who take over the series should be known as the "Mass Effect collective," and assert "governing rules around the IP.".

It's hard to imagine EA being willing to sell one of its franchises to fans, especially through a Kickstarter that would need some hefty investment. A self-governing body of fans is also admittedly a messy way to handle an IP — rather than it being bought back directly by veteran talent or other dev teams who could spearhead latest games under a more structured vision. With that being said, Hale remains optimistic about her idea, and suggests that a small portion of whatever the community makes could even go into "a fund that helps displaced devs.".

In a recent development, "EA can't buy that kind of publicity," she stated. "You cannot buy that kind of goodwill. The love that people and appreciation people would have for you for a long time, and the hats off to you would be invaluable. I have a business degree, and there is such a thing on the books called goodwill, and it is invaluable.".

Mass Effect trilogy director Casey Hudson, however, thinks that the impact from fans will look a little different. He recently said that he remains "optimistic" about the future of the series, and believes that the outpouring of support from the community will pave the way for its "triumphant return", pushing EA to do something with it in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next substantial game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game rapidly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

Recent findings suggest that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

According to recent reports, like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco revealed in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening.
  • The press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year.
  • In a recent development, bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now.

As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco revealed in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business looks, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation.".

The press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the manufacturer. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

In a recent development, bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is presently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

📅 04 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
  • The two latest features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
  • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis confirmed The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two upcoming destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two latest features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Recent findings suggest that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature introduces, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a upcoming virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

Recent findings suggest that it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In a recent development, in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the upcoming features, Maxis mentioned that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#17397. 7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1216 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way.
  • Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases.
  • Sources indicate that when I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way. While modern titles keep several staples of the genre, such as a fixed story, a focus on character development, innovation in the battle system, and some wacky progression systems, sometimes it feels like they leave behind certain mechanics that could be put to great use today. Many JRPGs of yesteryear featured unique mechanics that were either never re-explored, or, if they were, remained confined to indie games and flew under the radar of many players.

Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases. Most are battle-related, though a few, if properly implemented, could expand exploration and even improve how the game's systems interact. That is not to say they have never appeared in other games throughout the years, but I would love to see them become much more mainstream.

Sources indicate that when I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing. When chaining attacks, you can aim at enemies' limbs, yet all I ever did was try to go straight for the head or body to defeat the foe as fast as possible. How naive I was, because against bosses, that mindless strategy never paid off, especially if I was not wielding an appropriate weapon.

This mechanic of targeting different body parts has popped up in other JRPGs, though usually you can only hit distinct areas when an enemy is preparing a specific attack. I would love to see a JRPG reuse this mechanic exhaustively, letting players willingly target different enemy limbs and trigger distinct tactical outcomes.

In a recent development, one of Star Ocean's greatest strengths is its Item Creation system. To me, gaining levels wasn't about learning new combat skills, but it was all about earning points to invest in Customization and unlock new crafting potential, whether forging an endgame weapon at the start of the game or diving into other side activities. Still, the most entertaining feature, even at the cost of my relationship with my party members, was Pickpocketing.

According to recent reports, leveling up your Pickpocketing skill lets you steal from every NPC in town and score the wildest variety of items. The sheer thrill of not knowing what you would get, whether a simple consumable or an insanely overpowered piece of gear, was endlessly fun and had me making the rounds through town as if I were living inside GTA. As mentioned, doing so affects how your party members perceive the protagonist, so if you are aiming for a specific ending, watch out for the consequences of your actions.

This entry is less about battle mechanics and more about dungeon delving. As much as I love modern JRPGs, especially for their evolution in combat gameplay, narrative, and character development, I feel some are still a bit lacking in the level design department. Too many dungeons are simply streamlined corridors, featuring an occasional puzzle that solves itself before you even begin thinking through the solution.

Plenty of classic JRPGs boasted incredible level design, but if I had to highlight just one, it would be Wild Arms. This series blended the interactive tools of action-adventure games and let the scope of exploration expand incrementally. Moreover, acquiring fresh tools encouraged backtracking and re-exploring older dungeons, much like a Metroidvania, to hunt down hidden treasures.

Recent findings suggest that I never had much contact with Sega consoles growing up, which led me to neglect their JRPG catalog for quite a while. I played Phantasy Star IV fairly recently, and during my playthrough, a friend told me to set up Macros using specific skills while emphasizing that the execution order mattered. So I complied, and when I stepped into battle, oh boy, what a beautiful surprise.

Sources indicate that for those who don't know, depending on the sequence in which you cast spells and skills, they fuse together to unleash an entirely new combo attack. It is a deeply entertaining combo system that later surfaced in future JRPGs like Breath of Fire IV. It feels distinct from two characters simply chaining standard turns together, because there is a real sense of mystique in discovering the combinations, and I will confess that without a GameFAQs guide, I never would have figured them all out. Still, it is pretty amazing and elevated turn-based combat to new heights.

Recent findings suggest that staying on the topic of skill combos, Chrono Trigger pulled off something similar yet distinctly its own. If two or three party members mastered specific techniques and had their ATB gauges filled simultaneously, they could execute a Double or Triple Tech, each carrying a unique effect. The very first time I discovered this, as I imagine most players did, was with Crono and Lucca's Fire Whirl. A whole upcoming world of tactical possibilities opened up in that exact moment.

Chrono Trigger pushed the concept even further, and just when I expected the game to stick to Double Techs, the JRPG introduced Triple Techs. I don't know about you, but I built my entire party around these Techs, and luckily, nearly every character paired well with the rest of the roster. Triple Techs were slightly more restrictive, yet they still allowed for remarkably efficient setups, especially when hunting for Techs capable of healing the entire party at once.

According to recent reports, breath of Fire is my favorite JRPG series, and within it, Breath of Fire III stands as my absolute favorite entry. Whenever people ask me why, a massive part of my reasoning rests on its Gene splicing system, a feature Breath of Fire IV dropped for reasons I still don't understand, which was a real shame. I loved transforming into dozens of distinct dragons, even if Ryu and Fou-Lu's half-dragon forms looked awesome in their own right.

Recent findings suggest that essentially, you discovered Dragon Genes scattered across the world and could combine up to three at once to transform Ryu into wildly different dragon forms, each boasting unique strengths and abilities. The thing is, I don't necessarily need the exact Gene system back, but I would love a transformation-focused JRPG where characters can shift forms mid-battle and completely alter the flow of combat. Even better if those transformations feature distinct variations that actively reward exploration.

Recent findings suggest that I know there are many, many caveats surrounding the progression mechanics of Final Fantasy VIII, though I feel the bulk of player complaints stems from the Draw system rather than the Junction system itself. There is a historical reason behind that, as Hiroyuki Ito, creator of both the ATB and Junction systems, left the Final Fantasy VIII team before finalizing the battle mechanics to direct Final Fantasy IX, leaving his original vision somewhat incomplete.

Just imagine what it could have been if fully realized. The Junction system is remarkably dynamic. Beyond simply slotting spells to boost each character's raw stats, you could attach status ailments to basic physical attacks, build elemental resistances, tailor one character toward magic and agility while turning another into a pure strength powerhouse, and so on. Pair that flexibility with specialized commands learned through Guardian Forces, and what appears on the surface to be standard turn-based combat suddenly gains deep strategic layers.

  • Sources indicate that to find the Shrewsbury SM-69, head to the tall concrete watchtower near the starting location of GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 is full of things to see and questionable decisions to make, but you'll want to make sure you're properly armed before getting too carried away in Leonida. If you're looking to expand your weapon collection, getting your hands on a sniper rifle is a pretty good place to start.

It has been revealed that the Shrewsbury SM-69 is a handy addition to your arsenal, as it has impressive range and accuracy. You won't need to spend a fortune to add this weapon to your collection. I'll detail just exactly where to find it, below.

Sources indicate that to find the Shrewsbury SM-69, head to the tall concrete watchtower near the starting location of GTA 6. You can find it to the northwest of Nifty Threads Island Wear and just to the east of Pay 'n' Spray - Key Lento.

Recent findings suggest that once you reach the watchtower, you'll need to hop over the fence to access the area. I did not encounter any guards or enemies here, so you should be able to walk straight inside without any trouble.

Sources indicate that once inside the concrete building, climb the stairs and continue up the two sets of ladders. Here, you'll find the Shrewsbury SM-69 Sniper Rifle waiting for you to collect. The weapon has 6.8 damage, 8.6 accuracy, 2.0 handling, and 8.9 range, which makes it a useful addition to your weapon collection.

Make sure you add the Shrewsbury SM-69 to your car loadout (in the trunk) after picking it up so you can save the weapon and keep it available. You can also find some additional loot on the railing, including Cigarettes and Zombix.

If you continue climbing all the way to the top of the watchtower, you'll find a parachute waiting for you. It's worth making the extra climb if you want to grab another useful item before heading back down.
