  • One of the strangest is a large mutated crab you can find in the swamps that feels like something ripped out of the Fallout games.
  • Recent findings suggest that to start, make your way south to Pelican Valley in the Gullet Marsh region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in Grand Theft Auto 6, you will spend quite a bit of time ascending the criminal ladder, maintaining Jason and Lucia's relationship, and exploring Leonida. Unsurprisingly, there are a lot of weird things and people you can come across while exploring in and around Vice City.

One of the strangest is a large mutated crab you can find in the swamps that feels like something ripped out of the Fallout games. If you're looking to find this mutated crustacean and wondering what you will get for your troubles, here is how to find the giant crab, get the legendary Crabshack SMG, and find all the codes for the research lab.

Recent findings suggest that to start, make your way south to Pelican Valley in the Gullet Marsh region. Located around the center of the swamp (circled above) is a lone research station that you can dock your boat next to. If you're struggling to find it, I recommend looking for the building with all the tall antennas sticking out of it, as this can act as a visual marker for where the station is.

It has been revealed that additionally, you can visit this area as soon as you can freely roam around as Jason. It's relatively close to his home, making it a nice place to grab a great early-game legendary weapon; however, I recommend leaving the Stash Bag there since you won't be able to sell Marked Bills till later in the game. There's no combat or anything required to enter, as you won't actually be fighting the mutated crab.

Recent findings suggest that once you arrive at the research station, don't bother heading inside just yet. Instead, go around the back of the large house and look for a breaker box on the wall. Approach and interact with the box to restore power to the building. Now go inside the research station and head down the short hallway into the scientist's bedroom.

On the floor near the door are some words carved into the wood. Hold down the Left Trigger when near it to examine the writing and make note of the word CLEAVES that is at the bottom. Once you've examined it, return to the living room and approach the computer in the corner.

It has been revealed that interact with the computer to be prompted to enter the password on the right side of your screen. Select the word "CLEAVES" to gain access to the scientist's notes. There will be a section that states "SAFE CODE = DOUBLE SUCCESS." Once you're done reading, exit the computer to trigger a cutscene where a monstrous crab will attack you.

Recent findings suggest that fight it off via mashing the Square (PlayStation) / X (Xbox) button, and then leave the main building. Go back to where the breaker box was and look for a shack behind the house. Inside, you will find a bunch of terrariums where the crabs were being studied.

Recent findings suggest that specifically, look for a room with a much larger terrarium and examine the clipboard on the table next to it. You'll see that crab 36 was the one that was a success, meaning the code to the safe inside of the research station is 0072.

In a recent development, we get this number because the note on the computer states that the code is DOUBLE SUCCESS, meaning you need to double the number of the crab that survived the experiment. Inside the safe, you will find another note about an emergency protocol and $1,100 to spend.

We're not done yet. After you open the safe, head outside of the main building and look for a metal gate you can walk through along the wall (shown below). Follow the path to another shack on the water and enter the code 0212 at the door to open it.

Next to the body of the scientist, you'll find a Stash Bag with $10,000 Marked Bills and the Crabshack VF5 legendary submachine gun. If you're visiting here early, leave the Stash Bag to grab once you can sell the Marked Bills. You can then open the garage door, allowing you to drive the jet ski out!

Recent findings suggest that remember, once you grab this legendary weapon, it's part of your arsenal forever. You can always pick it up again at any weapons locker throughout the game, so it's a great firearm to snag early to make combat a little easier.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next massive game has officially introduced. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

It has been revealed that in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

According to recent reports, marathon has now officially released, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Industry observers note that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

In a recent development, indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game right now sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are presently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business concerns they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's notable to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing promptly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

In a recent development, essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 had a stellar launch, with two million XBOX players swarming to Newly introduced Zealand to start their playthrough as early as possible, boasting eye-watering sales figures, and breaking viewership records.

According to recent reports, bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful. One GTA 6 glitch that is gathering a lot of attention is one that lets players access a first-person mode.

As expected, GTA 6 is played in third-person and although many players appreciate a first-person mode, it is absent at launch, or at least, officially.

There is a glitch that enables a first-person look. It can be a little fiddly at first, but once you get the hang of it, you will have a better view at the sights. We have all the details you need to know about how to enter first-person mode the next time you load up the game.

Recent findings suggest that youTuber OneBoyler posted a video demonstrating how to do the GTA 6 first-person glitch on PlayStation. To perform the glitch, pause the game and go to the in-game settings, under the Controller tab, scroll down until you see Touch Pad Button. Change the Touch Pad Button to Camera 2. This setting changes your touchpad from opening the map to altering your camera view.

According to recent reports, next, sit in the driver’s seat of a vehicle and take out your mobile phone by pressing up on the D-Pad. Put your phone away by hitting circle on a PlayStation controller and then instantly spam your touchpad button.

Once successful, you will see the world from your character’s perspective, holding the wheel of the car. From this point onward, you can safely exit the car with first-person view intact and even access your loadout. Equipping a gun allows you to hold it realistically, and the animations are compatible with first-person mode.

Bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful.

Recent findings suggest that also, you can drive in first-person, bringing a new level of immersion to the already gorgeous and detailed world around you. The city lights reflecting off the front of your car hit different when you’re cruising around the streets.

It has been revealed that it’s worth noting that to return to third-person mode, you must reload your save. Make sure you save at the right time and don’t make any progress you want to risk losing while experimenting with the first-person view.

Industry observers note that when GTA 5 released on XBOX 360 and PlayStation 3 back in 2013, a first-person mode was absent. Only when GTA 5 was ported to XBOX One, PlayStation 4, and PC did a first-person perspective arrive in the game. Included were an optional first-person cover system, a newly introduced targeting system, traditional FPS controls, and fresh animations that allowed players to see the world in a whole new way.

In a recent development, if history were to repeat itself, a first-person mode could be on the cards for GTA 6 in a future update. For now, if you want to explore Leonida in first-person, you’ll have to do so using the glitch.

It’s unknown what the first post-launch GTA 6 patch will entail, but if it doesn’t bring a first-person mode with it, players will be hoping that Rockstar Games decides against patching out this particular bug.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related complications.

According to recent reports, today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

In a recent development, to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

In a recent development, the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Sources indicate that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

Recent findings suggest that in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

In a recent development, speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

It has been revealed that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Recent findings suggest that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

According to recent reports, sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

According to recent reports, for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a upcoming name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

#17370. Tech Report: Shrek 2 Remastered Fails To Capture The Magic Of Its Source Material

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (862 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Shrek 2 Remastered Fails To Capture The Magic Of Its Source Material

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I first heard the announcement for Shrek 2 Remastered, I couldn’t wait to get my hands on it.
  • In a recent development, to this day, I’m still a major sucker for licensed games, so revisiting a modern version of a classic wasn’t even a question.
  • While there are plenty of games that benefit from the traditional remaster treatment of updating visuals while leaving gameplay mostly unchanged, Shrek 2 likely would’ve been better off with the reverse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I first heard the announcement for Shrek 2 Remastered, I couldn’t wait to get my hands on it. As I’m sure many of you can relate to, movie tie-in games were a major part of my childhood. While the rest of my family rented their favorite films from Blockbuster, I always made a beeline for the games section, where I eventually discovered one of the best licensed games from the early 2000s, Shrek 2.

In a recent development, to this day, I’m still a major sucker for licensed games, so revisiting a modern version of a classic wasn’t even a question. Now that I’ve played it, however, I’m left wondering if a PS5 port of the original would’ve been a better option. While this is a remaster, not a full remake, playing it back-to-back with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) has been a jarring and eye-opening experience that highlights the right and wrong ways to bring back a beloved game from the past.

While there are plenty of games that benefit from the traditional remaster treatment of updating visuals while leaving gameplay mostly unchanged, Shrek 2 likely would’ve been better off with the reverse.

Industry observers note that despite their age, Shrek 2’s original graphics had their own charm, whereas improvements to character responsiveness could’ve transformed the game into a great experience for both new and returning players. Instead, Shrek 2 Remastered retains the same frustrating controls while the visuals have become something unsettling at best and downright nightmarish at worst.

Little Red, also known as Lil’ Red, was almost entirely left out of the marketing for Shrek 2 Remastered, to the point that many believed she’d been removed entirely. Now it’s a bit clearer why that decision might’ve been made. Most of the characters have a disturbing look to them now, but Lil’ Red’s makeover is certainly the most terrifying.

Characters' softer features and movie-accurate appearances have been replaced by lifeless eyes, intense contrast, and enhanced details, leaving them almost unrecognizable compared to their appearances in the 2004 release and the movie it’s based on. I'm also left wondering why so much effort was put into redesigning characters when the cutscenes haven't been formatted to fill the screen and are often cut off before they're finished.

Though the visuals were certainly disappointing, I might’ve been able to overlook them if they'd been accompanied by upcoming gameplay, but that remains unchanged. Most stages feature four characters that a solo player or a group of players can switch between to complete the required tasks.

Recent findings suggest that nearly every character is needed over the course of a single level due to their unique abilities, preventing one player from steamrolling others through the game. However, it also means solo players will be forced to use characters with less favorable controls.

Aside from Lil’ Red, who is actually somewhat enjoyable to play, thanks to her ranged apple throws and more fluid movements, most characters have limited attack ranges and feel stiff and unresponsive. Additionally, you’ll likely find yourself swapping characters more often than necessary because trailing characters (usually Shrek) frequently get stuck on obstacles and can’t free themselves.

Perhaps the one thing still saving this remaster from being a complete disappointment for me is that I’m playing local co-op with my partner, which has been fun simply because the game is so unforgiving. On more than one occasion, we’ve had to repeat a level multiple times to the point of delirious laughter. It’s not difficult, per se, but the lack of lives and poor controls make it brutal nonetheless.

In a recent development, unfortunately, all the aforementioned issues make it difficult to imagine upcoming players getting much enjoyment out of this remaster. Some older fans may be able to overlook the subpar gameplay in favor of nostalgia and the chance to play the game again, but I am finding it difficult. I’m grateful to have the opportunity to experience it on modern consoles with my partner, but that’s where my enjoyment ends.

It has been revealed that if you’re a fresh player curious about the hype surrounding the original, this remaster isn’t the way to discover it, and I’d recommend skipping it. On the other hand, if you’re a returning player eager to revisit the game and have no way to play the 2004 version, this will scratch the itch. If you do opt to play, however, I’d insist on playing multiplayer. Shrek 2 has always been better as a shared experience, but that’s especially true now in Shrek 2 Remastered.

Players do need to sign in to their Epic account to access multiplayer, which has been a major point of frustration for those playing on Steam in particular, so keep that in mind.

Overall, I’m walking away from Shrek 2 Remastered heartbroken. Had it received the full remake treatment with refined mechanics and a visual overhaul that enhanced rather than stripped away its original charm, this could have been an incredible experience for everyone to enjoy together. As it stands right now, however, I’m just left wishing I had a copy of the original game.

Recent findings suggest that the Sims 4 will soon get a newly introduced update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

According to recent reports, you can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

It has been revealed that going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

According to recent reports, speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis remarked this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently declared that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

Grand Theft Auto 6 might take players to a fictional version of Florida, but its success is apparently something the British government is more than happy to claim! After more than 10 years of anticipation, Rockstar’s latest blockbuster has finally arrived in the UK, and Downing Street has already found a reason to celebrate.

Oh, but there's just one small problem: Prime Minister Andy Burnham won't be joining the party, as his schedule is apparently a little too packed for a trip to Vice City.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday (thanks, The Independent), a Downing Street spokesperson described Rockstar Games as a "British success story made in Edinburgh," adding that many fans were already saying GTA 6 had been worth the wait.

When asked whether Burnham would be playing the game himself, however, the response was considerably less enthusiastic: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

It's a pretty amusing contrast, especially considering just how many people in the UK have been making room in their schedules for Rockstar's upcoming release! But hey, I get him – we’re talking about an experience that easily will get hold of 100+ hours of your life.

Sources indicate that although GTA 6 is set in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida, a significant part of the game's development took place in Scotland. Rockstar North, the studio responsible for much of the franchise's development, is based in Edinburgh, making the government's description of the game as a British success story more than just a bit of patriotic enthusiasm.

When asked whether Burnham would be playing the game himself, however, the response was considerably less enthusiastic: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

It has been revealed that the studio has been one of the UK's most recognizable names in the gaming industry for years, and GTA 6's launch is another major achievement for the country's game development scene. After all, it's not every day that one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in the world comes from a studio with such a strong presence in the UK, right?

Still, Burnham's absence from the player count might be a little disappointing for anyone hoping to see the Prime Minister share his first impressions of Vice City. At least Downing Street has made its position clear: the game is worth celebrating, even if its leader won't be playing it.

While Burnham apparently has more pressing matters to attend to, plenty of other people in the UK have found a way to squeeze GTA 6 into their day! A poll commissioned by Uswitch earlier this month estimated that around 2.8 million UK adults would play the game on launch day alone, with many expected to take annual leave or even call in sick to work.

The game's arrival has also prompted schools to remind students that its release isn't an excuse to skip lessons. GTA 6 carries an 18 age rating, and some schools have even introduced prize draws for vouchers among students who attend classes, hoping to keep attendance numbers up during the launch frenzy!

Honestly, it's hard to imagine a better illustration of just how substantial this release has become. Rockstar has managed to turn a video game launch into an event significant enough to reach Downing Street, spark discussions about school attendance, and even inspire millions of people to rearrange their schedules.

Burnham might not be joining Jason and Lucia on their adventures, but at least he can take comfort in knowing that a major British studio is behind one of the biggest games of the year. And, judging by the number of people taking the day off, his diary might be the only thing keeping him away from Vice City.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • General producer at P-Studio, Kazuhisa Wada, claims that Atlus has been working to reduce the time players have to wait between numbered entries in the long-running Persona series.
  • According to recent reports, in an interview as part of Sega Sammy's Samania series, which has been translated by GamesRadar+, Wada talks about how long it takes to create a numbered entry in the Persona series.
  • Persona 6 has already been more than five years in the works as it began development in 2021, following the global release of Persona 5 Royal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

General producer at P-Studio, Kazuhisa Wada, claims that Atlus has been working to reduce the time players have to wait between numbered entries in the long-running Persona series. Persona 6 doesn't currently have a release window, and it has already been more than a decade since Persona 5 first launched.

According to recent reports, in an interview as part of Sega Sammy's Samania series, which has been translated by GamesRadar+, Wada talks about how long it takes to create a numbered entry in the Persona series. "Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he explains. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

Persona 6 has already been more than five years in the works as it began development in 2021, following the global release of Persona 5 Royal.

Industry observers note that later in the interview, Wada hints that Atlus has been working in a way that will speed up the releases of numbered entries, though he doesn't make it clear how this will be achieved. "We are currently working on Persona 6," he says. "I can't say much at the moment, but we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

"Persona 6 is not the end," he continues. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day. Please look forward to more from the Persona series in the future.".

It's unclear whether Persona 6 is being developed concurrently with the next entry, or if Atlus is developing tools that can be used across multiple titles, but hopefully we won't be waiting another decade for Persona 7.

Persona 6 producer doesn't want "to make games for the global market," only something "we ourselves genuinely find exciting.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We interrupt your Grand Theft Auto 6 playtime to bring you the following announcement: there are more games launching today.

Yes, while 19th November 2026 will forever be known as 'GTA 6 Day ', a handful of other games are also braving the launch window and are releasing on Switch today.

According to recent reports, we know that your adventures in Leonida will take priority, and that's okay, but we thought it was only right to highlight the other experiences that didn't back down from the substantial boy's launch plans. And no, we're not highlighting everything launching on Switch today, since, well, the eShop is always bombarded with questionable titles that probably aren't worth checking out.

If, however, you're on the hunt for something with fewer Vice City vibes, here are some other options launching today.

There's every chance that you have already played through Bedtime Digital's Figment and Figment 2: Creed Valley when they launched on Switch 1 a few years back, but the Switch 2 versions are also launching today with some neat performance bumps. We're talking 60fps at 1080p and "enhanced graphics". Sounds ripe for a replay, if you ask us.

Published and developed by room6, this is a roguelike all about gathering cute pixel art plushies to your aid and using their powers to survive a nighttime onslaught of monsters. Need we say more? It seems to strike that balance of cute/creepy pretty well, and we can see it being quite the time sink, with 40 recruitable plushies, 100 items and 20 costumes available to mix up every run.

According to recent reports, those who frequent Japanese merch stalls will no doubt recognise the Sumikkogurashi gang. This one sees the team of adorable little blobs tasked with helping out at onsen inns to ensure their smooth running. There's plenty of minigames and scope to expand the inns further, but come on, the cuteness is the big draw here. Just look at those little guys!

In a recent development, it's The Binding of Isaac again (again). This re-release features all of the game's DLC content and the chance to play it with up to four players online.

Industry observers note that desperate for more throwback shooting after breezing through Boltgun? Auroch Digital has got you covered. After launching on other consoles last month, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun 2 finally arrives on Switch 2 today with even more strafing, shooting and scary monstrosities. The score features a surprise cameo track from composer Mick Gordon (DOOM, DOOM Eternal, Wolfenstein: The Upcoming Order), which is an added bonus for music fans.

It has been revealed that naturally, the eShop will be home to many more debuts today, but the above selection gives a pretty good range of options (and a certain quality that a bunch of the other releases lack). Let us know in the comments if there's another newbie today that we've missed!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

Industry observers note that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

According to recent reports, that same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Industry observers note that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

GTA’s Tool Choice Over Milwaukee Gives DeWalt Fans Bragging Rights

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A big part of what’s giving Grand Theft Auto 6 its incredible hypnotic power over a statistically-significant portion of the gaming public is its gigantic, intricately-designed world.
  • Early in the game, after receiving word that one of the game’s protagonists, Lucia, is coming back from prison, our other lead, Jason, can work to fix up their bungalow home in order to preemptively improve his relationship level with her.
  • According to recent reports, A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A big part of what’s giving Grand Theft Auto 6 its incredible hypnotic power over a statistically-significant portion of the gaming public is its gigantic, intricately-designed world. There are so, so many details to uncover all over the place if you take a moment to stop and look for them, and I’m not just talking about Bigfoot hanging out in the swamps or the many varieties of bird flying around. There are lots of little details that subtly inform aspects of the characters’ personalities and interests, including, apparently, the particular brands of power tools they prefer.

Early in the game, after receiving word that one of the game’s protagonists, Lucia, is coming back from prison, our other lead, Jason, can work to fix up their bungalow home in order to preemptively improve his relationship level with her. This means undertaking a few assorted tasks like repainting and fixing the walls, re-shingling the roof, fixing the stairs, and so-forth.

According to recent reports, A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow. The brand printed on the tool may be different from real-life, but fans of hardware know the distinct iconography of DeWalt when they see it.

It has been revealed that for those with no interest in power tools, DeWalt is one of the most prominent brands in the scene, manufacturing all of the usual implements like power drills, nail guns, circular saws, and all that other good stuff, usually powered by rechargeable battery packs. As is so often the case with this sort of thing, fans of DeWalt have something of an unofficial rivalry with fans of other major hardware brands, especially Milwaukee, whose tools are usually colored red.

It has been revealed that during Jason’s various household repair chores, he uses a couple of power tools colored the same shade of yellow as DeWalt’s, both emblazoned with the logo “DEVICE.” Obviously, Rockstar can’t just use DeWalt’s actual logo in its game without its permission (though I have a feeling DeWalt would’ve loved it if given the opportunity), but the particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable. Looks like Jason is a DeWalt man, and fans on the DeWalt subreddit are holding this up as a victory over the likes of Milwaukee.

The particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable.

Sources indicate that the particular implements that Jason uses seem to be at least partially inspired by real-life DeWalt tools. The driver he uses when fixing the walls is nearly identical to DeWalt’s 20V MAX 1/4 inch impact driver. The nail gun he uses to fix the fencing and roof doesn’t seem to have as close of a parallel, but it most closely-resembles the DeWalt 20V MAX XR brad nailer. That’s not a roofing-specific nailer, though, so either I’m wrong or Jason just doesn’t differentiate between nailer types. I’d believe either scenario.

While this may seem like a granular detail to hyperfixate on, as I mentioned, it’s just kind of fun to examine every aspect of this simulated world. In addition to what I said before about a character’s hardware preferences, it’s also interesting to hold up these simulated knock-off brands next to the real world.

Sources indicate that A massive part of the long-established aesthetic of the GTA world is riffing on aspects of real life. It’s always been a very exaggerated setting, often exemplifying the absolute worst parts of modern society for both laughs and drama. The fictional state of Leonida is pretty much Florida if it was slightly worse, and the same goes for Vice City and Miami.

In a recent development, GTA has also parodied more than its fair share of real-life brands and corporations over its various entries, usually with much sillier, ruder names. Sprite becomes “Sprunk,” IKEA becomes “KRAPEA,” and Twitter becomes “Bleeter,” which I am sincerely happy did not change its name to “Blex” or something equally stupid since GTA 5.

Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was declared in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

Industry observers note that when it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

It has been revealed that once downloaded, you’ll find a latest Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Industry observers note that once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the newly introduced Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

Sources indicate that all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

According to recent reports, the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

Sources indicate that this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big fresh revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, deadlock has already received numerous content updates and limited-time events to help spice up the pre-release gameplay experience, but several of the best creations for Valve's newest shooter are thanks to the community itself. On top of the countless skins, quality-of-life fixes, and trainers, some players have already created full-blown modes paying homage to Deadlock's predecessors.

With Deadlock having finally surpassed Team Fortress 2's peak player count thanks to its recent hero additions, the latest fan-made game mode bringing Prop Hunt to the game feels perfectly timed.

Although it's not an official game mode like Street Brawl, the mod created and shared by Jetsworm on X fully recreates the classic experience of hunting down players hiding as objects with an impressive level of quality.

Allowing up to 32 players in a single match, the hide-and-seek style mode offers over 150 props to choose from when hiding, fully refined rotation, and several locked-off areas you'll need to either hide or hunt through as opposed to scouring the entire map for hours. Rather than having to host it yourself, the mod custom game mode also has official servers for you to play on either with your friends or random players online.

If you want to try it out for yourself, you'll need to take the following steps to set up Deadlock's prop hunt mode before hopping in to play:.

On top of being completely free to play, the custom mode also offers points for each round you complete, which you'll then be able to spend on nameplate cosmetics for effects like changing its color, glow, background, and even animation style.

If you've never played Prop Hunt for yourself and are wondering what all the hype is about, the game mode that originates all the way back to Quake in the 90s before seeing its full success in Team Fortress 2 splits you up between a team that can take the image of objects to hide and hunters tasked with finding and killing them before time runs out.

Despite the simple premise, Prop Hunt has been ported to numerous games over the years, even beyond Valve's own Source Engine games, with franchises like Call of Duty recreating the mode with the release of Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, showing that the mode still offers timeless fun today.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam.
  • The dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart.
  • The next significant release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, update 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam. At the same time, the game has also been on the receiving end of criticism for its rather limited arsenal.

The dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart. After addressing the two more glaring omissions by adding the American M14 and the Soviet SKS, the most iconic Western weapon of the Cold War is finally making its way to Southeast Asia.

The next significant release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, update 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.

Introduced in 1953, the FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

Chambered for the same 7.62x51mm NATO as the M14, M40 and M60 already in the game, the L1A1 SLR (Self-Loading Rifle) variant comes with a 20-round box magazine and is limited to semi-automatic fire. This was a design choice by Commonwealth clients, and really, unless you want to shoot down NVA planes while aiming at the horizon, you won’t notice the difference.

Industry observers note that in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, the L1A1 will be available to the United States & Allies faction to represent its service with Australian and Upcoming Zealander units deployed there. Unlike the M14, the new rifle won’t be available to the Rifleman role.

The FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

To use the L1A1, you’ll need to reach level 6 in one of the following roles:.

In a recent development, I want to caveat here that if you actually pick the L1A1 over the M60 while playing machine gunner, you are a bad person and your team will be short in firepower. MG roles are for pouring it on downrange, not for reloading after twenty shots, and I’m saying this as a staunch FAL defender.

The developers have not offered any insight on how the pilots are supposed to fit a rifle that long in the cockpit of the Huey, but we can look the other way for a little bit.

As much as I’m pining for the L1A1 and it will be my personal highlight of update 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, it’s hard to argue against the real big item on the prospective patch notes being the Khe Sanh map and what it means for the game as a whole.

Khe Sanh will be the debut map for the Assault game mode, doubling down on the attackers versus defenders gameplay already present in the Offensive mode.

In a recent development, assault brings back a fan favorite from the World War 2 Hell Let Loose, and focuses specifically on horrific trench warfare, strongpoints, and choosing whether you prefer dying in a fatal funnel in a trench or getting ripped apart by artillery out in the open. It’s great fun once you get used to the tinnitus.

Level designer Kienan Suthar provides more detail in this deep dive:.

The battle of Khe Sanh was one of the toughest battles in the Vietnam War, coinciding with the Tet Offensive of January 1968 and lasting until July of that same year.

Industry observers note that khe Sanh Combat Base was surrounded by a large North Vietnamese force, supported by Viet Cong and Pathet Lao rebels. For five months, US and allied forces reinforced the base primarily from the air, while throwing everything and the kitchen sink at the Vietnamese troops.

The outcome of the battle, as many major engagements of the Vietnam War, was inconclusive. The North Vietnamese siege was partially lifted by April 1968, but a shift in US strategy in the aftermath of the Tet Offensive led to its abandonment on July 9.

Recent findings suggest that for the Americans, avoiding a Điện Biên Phủ situation and preventing the collapse of the base was considered a win. The North Vietnamese, meanwhile, celebrated victory by capturing the region following the withdrawal.

For players, the real tangible outcome is that it created an incredibly dense network of fortifications for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam to sink its teeth into the assault mode.

Upgrade 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is scheduled for the first half of December. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is currently available on PC, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X/S.

Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.
  • The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be said for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.
  • In a recent development, it also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be said for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

In a recent development, it also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

If you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Recent findings suggest that ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

Recent findings suggest that batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

Steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

Sources indicate that however, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

Sources indicate that this one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

With a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

It also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

Industry observers note that having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

In a recent development, excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

Industry observers note that sadly, it's also a game which never launched in Europe, so we're presently tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

Look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

It has been revealed that hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

An engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the company filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

As a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

Honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

Keeping hold of Firm of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO indicates – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1081 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • According to recent reports, without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • Industry observers note that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

According to recent reports, without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Tech giant of Heroes provides.

Industry observers note that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

Industry observers note that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

According to recent reports, anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Manufacturer of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell claims. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

Sources indicate that relic and newly introduced owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Manufacturer of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent enhancement is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell notes foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very swiftly.".

In a recent development, I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had looks to release fresh games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Tech giant of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

It has been revealed that however, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding, buying, and stealing your dream car or bike is a peak part of Grand Theft Auto, and mine is the Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse in GTA 6, based on the bright green car driven by Paul Walker as Brian O'Conner in the original movie. This gorgeous motor can be found locked in a garage in Vice City in GTA 6, but it can be stolen, and, if you play your cards right, you can even register it as your own for free. Here's how.

To find Paul Walker's Fast and Furious Mitsubishi in GTA 6, you need to head towards Vice Beach, to the east of Vice City. The car is locked in a garage on Vespucci Island, one of the Rialto Islands to the west of Vice Beach. You can see the exact location marked on the map above.

You'll have to break into the garage and steal the car, which is actually a lot easier than it sounds, but I've got more details on that below.

As you'd expect, the Mitsubishi handles really well and hits high speeds, so it's one of the best GTA 6 cars you can get your hands on, especially in the early game, for free, and without picking up too much heat.

To steal Paul Walker's GTA 6 car, head to the garage and break in. This triggers an alarm, but you can switch that off pretty promptly on the wall to your left as you head in. Open the garage door here too, break into the car, hotwire it, and drive away - simple as that.

There are a few additional details to note here, though, that make this experience easier or better for you overall.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major upgrade. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the substantial focus of this revision, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot newly introduced arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this revision. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Industry observers note that ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

Industry observers note that if he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

According to recent reports, returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

In a recent development, version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Latest Update: Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards
